title: Assessment and observation words
blurb: Define the words for examining, measuring and observing a patient, from auscultate and palpate to patent, occult and lucid.
question: “The nurse auscultated the lungs, palpated the abdomen and confirmed the IV was patent; the patient was lucid and oriented.” If palpate looks like palpitate and patent looks like latent, how do you keep them straight under time pressure?

teach.body: Assessment words describe how a health worker gathers information: the exam techniques (auscultate, palpate, percuss), the kind of data (objective, subjective, sign, symptom, baseline), the state of a passage (patent, occluded) and the patient's mental state (lucid, coherent, oriented). Formally, they are the vocabulary of patient assessment. Plain English: they name how you check a patient and what you find.

teach.h: Sign or symptom? Objective or subjective?
teach.caption: A syndrome is a set of signs and symptoms that occur together.

head: Verb
Sense used
Look-alike trap
rows: ears: listen, often with a stethoscope
teach.caption: Assess (v) means to evaluate. Monitor (v) means to observe and check over time.

head: Word
Meaning
Near miss
rows: aware of self, place and time

teach.h: Scenario: Hannah reads an exam note
teach.body: Hannah, a nursing applicant volunteering at a community clinic, reads a note on Mr. Okafor: “Baseline blood pressure elevated. Lungs auscultated: clear. Abdomen palpated: soft. IV site patent. Stool positive for occult blood. Patient lucid, coherent and oriented. Reports nausea (subjective); no fever (objective).” She wants to explain each finding in everyday words.

items: Baseline elevated: the first blood pressure reading, used for comparison, was above normal.
Auscultated, palpated: the lungs were listened to; the abdomen was felt by hand.
Patent IV: the line is open. Occult blood: blood that cannot be seen with the eye.
Lucid, coherent, oriented: clear-headed, logical, and aware of self, place and time.
Nausea is subjective because he reports it; temperature is objective because it is measured.

teach.text: Palpate (feel by touch) is not palpitate (heart racing). Patent (open) rhymes with latent (inactive) and looks like potent (strong). Occult (hidden) is not occlude (block). And a sign is objective, seen or measured by someone else; a symptom is subjective, felt and reported by the patient.

items: Auscultate = listen; palpate = feel; percuss = tap; inspect = look.
Sign = objective, measurable; symptom = subjective, reported by the patient.
Patent = open; occlude = block; occult = hidden.
Lucid = clear-headed; coherent = logical; oriented = aware of self, place and time.
Baseline = first reading for comparison; elevated = raised; acuity = sharpness.

summary: You can now define the words for exam techniques, types of data, the state of a passage and a patient's mental status. You can also reject the HESI A2 look-alikes: palpate and palpitate, patent and latent, occult and occlude, sign and symptom.

A.q: The nurse will palpate Mr. Ito's wrist to count his pulse for a full minute. What is the best definition of the word “palpate” in this sentence?
A.why: Palpate means to examine by touching or pressing with the hands or fingers.

whyNot.3: Beating rapidly is palpitate, the look-alike.

A.q: Swelling around the insect bite was the first sign the nurse recorded during the visit. What is the best definition of the word “sign” in this sentence?
A.why: A sign is objective evidence of disease that someone else can observe or measure, such as swelling.

whyNot.0: A feeling the patient reports is a symptom.
whyNot.2: A set of related signs and symptoms is a syndrome.
whyNot.3: The cause of an illness is its etiology.

A.q: Ms. Ruiz's blood pressure was elevated at her first visit, so the nurse rechecked it before she left. What is the best definition of the word “elevated” in this sentence?

whyNot.1: Lowered below normal is depressed or low, the opposite.
whyNot.2: Eased or relieved is alleviated, a sound-alike.
whyNot.3: Taken away is eliminated, a look-alike.

B.q: During clinicals, the student nurse learned to auscultate bowel sounds in all four quadrants of the abdomen. What is the best definition of the word “auscultate” in this sentence?
B.why: Auscultate means to listen to sounds inside the body, usually with a stethoscope.

B.q: Although his fever was high, Mr. Diaz remained lucid throughout the admission interview. What is the best definition of the word “lucid” in this sentence?
B.why: Lucid means clear-headed and able to think clearly.

whyNot.1: Drowsy describes lethargy, nearly the opposite.
whyNot.2: Flushed describes skin color; livid, a look-alike, also describes color.

B.q: An occlusion in the artery to Mr. Brown's left leg caused cramping whenever he walked a block. What is the best definition of the word “occlusion” in this sentence?
B.why: An occlusion is a blockage or closing of a passage or vessel.

whyNot.0: A tear is a rupture, not a blockage.
whyNot.1: Hidden bleeding is occult blood, a look-alike word.
whyNot.2: An enlargement of an artery is an aneurysm, not an occlusion.

C.q: The nurse charted the patient's description of a “pressing” chest pain as subjective data. What is the best definition of the word “subjective” in this sentence?
C.why: Subjective means based on personal feelings or reports; the description comes from the patient.

whyNot.0: Measured by a device is objective.
whyNot.1: Confirmed by a test is objective.
whyNot.3: Something the nurse sees is objective, a sign.

C.q: Before starting the infusion, the nurse flushed the line to be sure it was patent. What is the best definition of the word “patent” in this sentence?
C.why: In a medical sentence, patent means open and unblocked.

whyNot.0: Inactive is latent, a rhyming look-alike.
whyNot.2: A line should be sterile, but flushing checks that it is open.

C.q: Hearing acuity declines gradually in many older adults, so the clinic offers yearly screenings. What is the best definition of the word “acuity” in this sentence?
C.why: Acuity is sharpness or keenness, especially of vision or hearing.

whyNot.0: Loudness is a property of sound, not of the listener's hearing.
whyNot.2: Balance is a separate inner ear function.

reteach.title: Checking a used car
reteach.question: Before buying a used car, you look it over, listen to the engine, feel the tires and knock on the panels. Isn't that a full assessment?

blocks.h: The car check is an exam
blocks.body: Looking at the paint is inspection. Listening to the engine idle is like auscultating. Running your hand over the tires is palpating. Knocking on a door panel to hear whether it is solid is percussing. The seller's story, “It runs great,” is subjective. The mileage on the dashboard is objective. A clear fuel line is patent; a clogged one is occluded.

blocks.text: Palpating the tires means feeling them, not your heart racing at the price. That racing is a palpitation.

explain.body: Objective data are observable facts and measurements, such as temperature. Subjective data are what the patient feels and reports, such as pain. Signs are objective; symptoms are subjective.

test.q: The nurse charted objective findings, including a temperature of 101°F and a swollen left ankle. What is the best definition of the word “objective” in this sentence?
test.why: Objective means based on observable facts and measurements.

whyNot.0: Based on the patient's feelings is subjective, the opposite.
whyNot.1: Open to argument is debatable or objectionable, not objective.
whyNot.3: A goal is the noun objective; the adjective describes the data.

explain.body: Inspect means to look. Auscultate means to listen. Palpate means to feel by touch. Percuss means to tap a surface and judge what lies beneath by the sound.

test.q: The physician will percuss over the right upper abdomen to estimate the size of the liver. What is the best definition of the word “percuss” in this sentence?
test.why: Percuss means to tap a body surface to judge what lies beneath by the sound.

explain.body: Patent means open and unblocked. Occlude means to block, and an occlusion is a blockage. Occult means hidden, as in blood too small in amount to see.

test.q: The yearly screening test checks for occult blood in the stool of adults over 45. What is the best definition of the word “occult” in this sentence?
test.why: In medicine, occult means hidden; not visible to the naked eye.

whyNot.1: Bright red blood is visible, the opposite of occult.
whyNot.2: Clotted blood has thickened; occult describes visibility.
whyNot.3: Excess describes amount, not whether it can be seen.

explain.body: Lucid means clear-headed. Coherent means clear and logical. Oriented means aware of who one is, where one is and the time. Cognitive means relating to thinking and memory.

test.q: The nurse documented that Mr. Okafor was awake, alert and oriented at the start of her shift. What is the best definition of the word “oriented” in this sentence?
options: aware of self, place and time
test.why: Oriented means aware of who one is, where one is and the time.

whyNot.0: Sitting upright describes position, not awareness.
whyNot.1: Calm and cooperative describes behavior, not orientation.
